knowledge_point.title: Differentiating the Product of a Constant and the Natural Logarithm Function

question.:question/worked-solution:
The derivative of the natural logarithm is the reciprocal function:

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\ln x)=\frac{1}{x}
$$

We apply our formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{\ln x}{4}\right) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{4}\,\ln x) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\ln x) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{x} \\  & =\frac{1}{4x}.\end{aligned}
$$
